_comment: tests/port/vram.py: the differences known and explained, by dump name (the same moment in every script) and check (vram, textures, frame). A listed check that differs is reported, not failed; one that is equal again is reported as stale (remove it). docs/PORT.md "Testing".

title.vram: 2 pixels, the mask bit only (the picture is equal): the title's rays, polygons modulated by black, cover them in one renderer and not the other (psxstack#54, 1)

title_menu.vram: x 286, 5 pixels per buffer, one colour step: the last column of the menu's 255-wide mode-2 modulated sprite (psxstack#54, 2)

_comment_aligned: The registration's and SAISEG's dumps, aligned on the game's state (vram.py ALIGN, EXTRA_DUMPS, END_DUMPS; #33): what is left is the software GPU against PCSX-Redux on stretched textured quads (a texture span one texel short of the screen span: one row or column of the quad takes the neighbouring texel), and one model animation

name_entry.vram: 65 pixels per buffer: one row or column of the stretched title parts (the tab bar's row 34, the logo's row 53, the Reception label's column 230) (psxstack#54, 3)

name_entered.vram: 77 pixels per buffer: one row or column of the stretched title parts (psxstack#54, 3)

starter_select.vram: 51 pixels per buffer: one row or column of the stretched title parts (the tab bar's row 34, column 220, column 75) (psxstack#54, 3)

starter_chosen.vram: the player's model in another pose: its looping idle animation starts with the page, so the wait for the scrolling background (the frames the loads took differ) puts it at another phase; aligned on the page instead, the model agrees and the background does not (#33); and the title parts' rows (psxstack#54, 3)

saiseg_area.vram: 157 pixels per buffer: one column or row of SAISEG's stretched quads (Beginner City's 254-wide picture with u 0..255: column 160; the frame's 40x40 tiles with uv spans of 39: row 30, column 18) (psxstack#54, 3)

saiseg_message.vram: 165 pixels per buffer: the same columns and rows as saiseg_area (psxstack#54, 3)
